results.content: The Strategic Council’s effort, which began in 2022, found that U.S. public confidence in science, the scientific community, and leaders of scientific communities is high relative to other civic, cultural, and governmental institutions for which researchers regularly collect such data. Ninety-two percent (92%) offer the same responses to scientists “being open to changing their minds based on new evidence.” Collectively, these data clarify how the U.S. public views science and scientists. Second, we describe findings from a newly developed approach to analyzing public confidence in science by asking detailed questions not just about science in general but also about perceptions both of scientists’ adherence to the scientific norms they espouse and of the incentives that motivate individual scientists and organizations. results.content: My responsibilities involve analyzing human subject research submissions to ensure they comply with applicable regulations, managing departmental billing, and organizing institutional and national conferences.I’m a proud member of the IRB Community Engagement & Outreach Unit, where I participate in community outreach efforts to engage our local community (and communities throughout the CSRA area) in meaningful conversations regarding human subject research at Augusta University and establish a collaborative relationship with the citizens we serve. Bianca Marsh, BA, serves as the Institutional Review Board Training & Education Coordinator at Augusta University, where she develops and implements training programs focused on the regulatory requirements for human subjects research. Joining the Augusta University Institutional Review Board Office in 2022 following various research support roles across multiple departments, she functions as a liaison and navigator for Augusta University/WHMCG researchers submitting to the IRB, providing current regulation and guidance to ensure human subject research protocols are complete and compliant.
